newsitem.title: CANADA: BOC's Thiessen cautions on maneuver room remarks.
newsitem.headline: BOC's Thiessen cautions on maneuver room remarks.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen cautioned on Friday against reading a specific course of action into his remarks that the central room had more room for maneuver in reaction to possible U.S. interest rate hikes.
"There will always be an impact on Canada of an international change in interest rates," Thiessen told reporters after a speech to economists.
"But the difference I think now is that we have got more room to maneuver than we did before. But you should not interpret that as saying what we are going to do next week or not," he added.
Thiessen also said he agreed with a forecast from Canada's Royal Bank, which predicted the creation of 700,000 new jobs in the next two years.

"I don't know if I want to make a specific forecast, but I think there is going to be a substantial increase in the amount of employment," Thiessen told reporters. "Those kinds of numbers certainly look to me like they could be possible."
Thiessen said the bank's flexibility has not been affected by the recent weakening in the Canadian dollar.
He said he was optimistic the currency would strengthen in the long run.

"No central banker likes to see a weak currency. A weak currency is all too often an indication it is not doing as well as your neighbor's," he said. "But I would say that I continue to believe there's an upward trend in the Canadian dollar."
The Canadian dollar was trading at C$1.3792 (US$0.7251) against the U.S. dollar by mid-afternoon Friday, down from recent peaks around C$1.33.
Thiessen said it was too soon to say if the weaker currency has loosened monetary conditions too much.
"We have ups and downs," he said. "You don't really respond to short-term changes like that."
Thiessen added that today's core consumer price was positive for the currency.
